Anonymous requests can ask for at most **20 results per page**, and the code's default rate limits for them are **5 requests/hour (burst) and 100 requests/day (sustained)**. Those rate numbers come from the code, though, not from a published limit, so production may be set differently.

- **Rate limits:** the `anon_burst` and `anon_sustained` defaults are read from environment variables (`THROTTLE_ANON_BURST`, `THROTTLE_ANON_SUSTAINED`), so the live API can override them. The official API docs don't publish anonymous thresholds, at least not in any page I could read. The schema only says unverified apps get "the same rate limits as an anonymous user." Two other anonymous limits in the code are thumbnails at 150/minute and healthcheck at 3/minute. Authenticated apps get 100/min and 10,000/day by default, and "enhanced" apps get 200/min and 20,000/day.
- **Page size:** `MAX_PAGE_SIZE` is 20 for anonymous requests, which is also the default, and 50 for authenticated ones. Anonymous and standard authenticated requests can both reach only 12 pages of 20, so 240 results per search.
- **Conflicting figure:** a search-engine summary gave "20 requests per minute and 200 per day" for anonymous access. I couldn't trace it to any Openverse source, so I'd treat it as unverified.
- **Older figure:** a 2022 post says anonymous users were throttled to 1 request/second before v2.5.5. That's outdated.

To see the limits that apply to you, call `GET /v1/rate_limit/`. The schema says it returns `requests_this_minute`, `requests_today` and `rate_limit_model`, but it needs an API key, so it won't help for anonymous traffic.

Sources:
- [api/conf/settings/rest_framework.py](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/WordPress/openverse/main/api/conf/settings/rest_framework.py): throttle rate defaults (main branch, read 2026-11-15)
- [api/api/constants/restricted_features.py](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/WordPress/openverse/main/api/api/constants/restricted_features.py): `MAX_PAGE_SIZE` 20 / 50 and the 240-result depth
- [api.openverse.org/v1/schema/](https://api.openverse.org/v1/schema/): `page_size` default 20, the `/v1/rate_limit/` endpoint, the unverified-app wording
- [github.com/WordPress/openverse/issues/4324](https://github.com/WordPress/openverse/issues/4324): 2024-05-14, closed, set the authenticated page size limit to 50
- [make.wordpress.org/openverse/2022/06/17/…](https://make.wordpress.org/openverse/2022/06/17/mitigating-out-of-terms-api-usage/): 2022, the 20-per-page cap since v2.5.5 and the old 1 request/second throttle

Anonymous requests to the Openverse API get **20 requests per minute (burst) and 200 requests per day (sustained)**. The largest page size they can ask for is **20** (`page_size` max 20).

- **Rate limits:** A third-party directory page states 20 requests/min burst and 200 requests/day sustained, and says it verified them on 2026-10-31. A GitHub issue from 2026-09-09 shows the matching response headers, `x-ratelimit-limit-anon_burst: 20/min` and `x-ratelimit-limit-anon_sustained: 200/day`. That issue is the closest thing to a primary source I found.
- **Page size:** Openverse's own 2022 announcement says that after API version 2.5.5, searches made without an API key cannot request more than 20 results per page. The directory page quotes the error as "page_size may not exceed 20 for anonymous requests".
- **Result depth:** A search summary (not a page I read) said anonymous users can see only the first 240 results of a search, which is 12 pages of 20. I haven't verified that.
- **Unconfirmed:** I couldn't read the official docs page at api.openverse.org, because it didn't render for my fetcher. The numbers therefore come from the issue headers and the directory page, not from the docs themselves.
- **Older figure:** The 2022 announcement says anonymous users are throttled to 1 request/second. That figure is old and doesn't match the current headers, so I'd discount it.
- **For comparison:** The search summary gave authenticated limits of 100/min and 10,000/day, and enhanced limits of 200/min and 20,000/day. I didn't confirm those on a page I read. The docs say the exact values can change.
- **Checking live:** Responses carry rate-limit headers, and a search summary says `/rate_limit` returns your remaining quota. I didn't confirm that endpoint on a page.

Sources:
- [Openverse issue #5613, rate-limit headers (2026-09-09)](https://github.com/WordPress/openverse/issues/5613)
- [Openverse API directory entry (verified 2026-10-31)](https://agentapilist.com/agent-tools/openverse-api/)
- [Openverse: mitigating out-of-terms API usage (2022)](https://make.wordpress.org/openverse/2022/06/17/mitigating-out-of-terms-api-usage/)
- [Openverse API docs: authentication and throttling](https://wordpress.github.io/openverse-api/reference/api/authentication_and_throttling.html) (no numbers on the page)

On the year: the release page shows "11 Nov" with no year, and GitHub drops the year only for dates in the current year. That makes it **2026**. Vite's latest stable version is 8.3.8, and it requires Node.js `^20.19.0 || >=22.12.0`. I couldn't confirm its release date.

- **Version:** 8.3.8 is the `version` field on `main` in the Vite repo's `package.json`, and the GitHub releases page also lists it as the latest stable release. The vite.dev releases page still showed 8.3.7, so it lags by one patch.
- **Node.js:** that same `package.json` has `"engines": {"node": "^20.19.0 || >=22.12.0"}`. That means 20.19.0 or higher on the 20 line, or 22.12.0 and above. The Vite 8 announcement says the same.
- **Release date:** unresolved. The GitHub releases fetch gave "November 11, 2024", but I don't trust it. Vite 8.0 only came out on March 12, 2026, so an 8.3.8 release in 2024 is impossible. The fetch summary probably got the year wrong. The likely date is 2026-11-11, but that's an inference. Check the date on the GitHub release page or npm.

I didn't find a source that states the date reliably.
